subject: Choice of law and urgent remedies — handoff for redlines
messages:
From: Michael Chen <mchen@auroramed.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: AuroraMed Procurement <procurement@auroramed.com>, AuroraMed Legal <legal@auroramed.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Redlined MSA + Order Form — governing law and emergency remedies

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. I attached our redlines to the MSA and the order form (MSA_AuroraMed_redlines.pdf, OrderForm_AuroraMed_v2.docx). Two items our legal/procurement teams flagged up front:

- Governing law: AuroraMed prefers Massachusetts law on the basis of precedent for our industry.
- Emergency remedies: we need clear carveouts for preliminary injunctive relief in any state or federal court where AuroraMed operates (primarily MA and NY). We are willing to go to arbitration for monetary claims but can’t accept arbitration-only for urgent compliance or patient-safety injunctive relief.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on a split approach (arbitration for damages, court carveout for injunctive relief) and whether you will accept MA as the governing law? If not, please propose language that would be acceptable for both sides.

Also: procurement asked whether a PO is required or if DocuSign will suffice.

We'd like to get alignment this week — happy to jump on a short call.

Best,
Michael
Michael Chen
Head of Legal Operations, AuroraMed
(attachment: MSA_AuroraMed_redlines.pdf)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Chen <mchen@auroramed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redlined MSA + Order Form — governing law and emergency remedies

Michael — thanks for sending these over and for the clear callouts. Looping in Ben (Sales) and Laura (Legal) to propose the cleanest path forward. A few quick notes while we prep language:

- We are open to a bifurcated approach: arbitration for most disputes, with an express carveout for equitable relief (injunctive/preliminary relief) to be sought in court.
- On governing law, Redwood's standard is California law (our principal place of business), but we're comfortable discussing a compromise. Would AuroraMed consider a clause that says: "This Agreement is governed by the law of the State of X, except that either party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction"? That preserves arbitration for damages while preserving urgent relief in court.

Laura — can you draft one or two short alternative clause options we can send Michael today (e.g., Redwood-friendly: CA law + injunctive carveout; middle-ground: neutral forum like Delaware or MA + injunctive carveout)?

Michael — happy to jump on a 20-min call if helpful. Ben, please confirm commercial cadence if AuroraMed is ready to sign once legal is aligned.

Thanks,
Grace
VP, Solutions — Redwood Inference
(attachment: OrderForm_AuroraMed_v2.docx)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Chen <mchen@auroramed.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redlined MSA + Order Form — governing law and emergency remedies

Grace / Michael — quick commercial note from our side: AuroraMed's timeline matters for our quarter close, so if legal clears language that preserves injunctive relief in courts and arbitration for monetary claims, we can proceed to signature quickly.

From a sales perspective we're comfortable offering a 30-day implementation credit if DocuSign is executed this week and PO follows within 10 business days. If AuroraMed prefers a neutral governing law (e.g., Delaware) rather than CA, we can be flexible — but we should lock the injunctive carveout.

Happy to take a 15m call to align terms and signature mechanics.

Ben
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Chen <mchen@auroramed.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed language for bifurcated dispute resolution (MSA §14)

Hi Michael — per Grace's note, attached is a short snippet with two alternative clauses (PI_clause_snippet.txt). Below is the redline-free text for clarity:

Option A (Redwood-preferred)
"This Agreement will be governed by the laws of the State of California, without regard to conflicts of law principles. Except as set forth below, any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement will be finally resolved by binding arbitration in accordance with the rules of the American Arbitration Association. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to prevent the actual or threatened infringement, misappropriation, or disclosure of Confidential Information or to preserve the status quo pending arbitration."

Option B (Middle-ground)
"This Agreement will be governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. Except as set forth below, any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement will be finally resolved by binding arbitration administered by the AAA. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief in any federal or state court of competent jurisdiction (including courts located in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts)."

A couple of practical points:
- We should explicitly reference which claims are arbitrable (typically all except equitable relief).
- If AuroraMed wants a requirement to seek injunctive relief first in a local court, that can be discussed but is unusual and may complicate enforcement.

If you prefer Option B (MA law), we will run a very short internal approval to accept MA law plus the carveout. If you prefer Option A, we can keep CA law and the same equitable-relief carveout.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
(attachment: PI_clause_snippet.txt)

From: Michael Chen <mchen@auroramed.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: AuroraMed Procurement <procurement@auroramed.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed language for bifurcated dispute resolution (MSA §14)

Thanks Laura — Option B (Massachusetts law + carveout) tracks closest to our internal mandate. Two clarifications from our side:

1) Seat/venue for arbitration: AuroraMed's preference is Boston, MA (to be reflected as "seat of arbitration" only for administrative purposes; substantive law would remain MA).
2) Injunctive relief carveout: we agree to the broad carveout you proposed, but want a short sentence clarifying that seeking injunctive relief in court does not waive the right to arbitration for any monetary claims.

If Redwood can sign up to those two points we will route to our GC for a quick sign-off and then use the DocuSign link for signature. Please confirm whether PO or DocuSign is sufficient — procurement would prefer DocuSign + PO to follow.

Michael
(attachment: none)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Chen <mchen@auroramed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Final alignment — MA law + arbitration seat in Boston; injunctive carveout confirmed

Michael — thank you, and appreciated the clear asks. Laura and I discussed internally; Redwood will accept Option B with the two clarifications you requested:

- Governing law: Commonwealth of Massachusetts.
- Arbitration: binding arbitration (AAA) with seat in Boston, MA for administrative purposes.
- Injunctive relief carveout: expressly preserved in federal or state court (MA or any court of competent jurisdiction) with a sentence confirming that seeking equitable relief does not waive the right to arbitrate monetary claims.

Ben confirms commercial steps: we will send a DocuSign packet for signature today. Execution via DocuSign is sufficient; AuroraMed can issue a PO within 10 business days per the credit terms Ben offered.

Next steps:
- Laura to incorporate agreed text and attach revised MSA for signature (will include PI_clause_snippet.txt integrated).
- Ben to generate DocuSign and share hubspot/deal updates (HS-654321).
- Grace to schedule a 15m kickoff for implementation once signed.

If that works, we'll route for signatures today. Thanks all.

Grace O'Connor
VP, Solutions — Redwood Inference
(attachment: MSA_AuroraMed_redlines_final.pdf)
